info.name: Traveler Guide API
info.description:
# Traveler Guide API

Generated from the services' own OpenAPI documents by
`scripts/generate-postman.py`, covering **144 operations** across
**14 services**. Re-run that script after changing a route so this
collection cannot drift from the code.

## Getting started

1. Start the stack: `pnpm dev:all`
2. Select the **Traveler Guide — Local** environment.
3. Run **02 · Auth · Public → Login (admin)**. It stores `accessToken` and
   `refreshToken` automatically; every other request inherits them.

## How requests reach a service

Everything goes through the gateway on `{{baseUrl}}` (`http://localhost:4000`).
The gateway routes on the first path element after `/v1` — `/v1/map/...` goes to
map-service, `/v1/auth/...` to auth-service — and forwards the path unchanged,
so the path you see here is the path the service sees.

The gateway also:

- **rejects anonymous requests** to anything outside its small public list
  (registration, login, refresh, forgot/reset password, health);
- **requires the `admin:access` permission** for every `/v1/*/admin/**` path;
- **returns 404 for every `/v1/*/internal/**` path**, so service-to-service
  endpoints can never be reached from outside;
- **strips client-supplied identity headers** and re-mints `x-user-id`,
  `x-user-email`, `x-user-roles` and `x-user-permissions` from the verified
  token, so a caller cannot impersonate anyone by setting a header;
- attaches an `x-correlation-id` to every request for tracing.

## Accounts

| Account | Credentials | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator | `admin@travelerguide.com` / `Admin@123456` | Users, Roles, Integrations, Database Admin |
| Traveler | `traveler@guide.test` / `Traveler@123` | Profile, Map, Assistant |

## Response shape

Every endpoint answers with the same envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": { } }
```

and on failure:

```json
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "UNAUTHORIZED", "message": "…" } }
```

## What is implemented

auth-service, user-service, map-service and ai-service carry real domain logic.
The other nine services are scaffolds: they expose health plus the generic table
editor, and their database holds a single placeholder `ServiceRecord` model.

item.name: Every service with its manageable tables, for the admin sidebar

request.description:
Every service with its manageable tables, for the admin sidebar

`GET /v1/admin/services`

**Auth:** bearer token **plus the `admin:access` permission**. Sign in with the admin account or the gateway answers 403.

item.description:
Liveness checks and service discovery.

`GET /v1/health` on the gateway reports only the gateway. The **Direct service health** requests bypass the gateway and hit each service on its own port, which is how you tell a dead service apart from a dead gateway.

`GET /v1/admin/services` is what the admin portal calls to build its sidebar: it returns every service with its tables and an `online` flag.

item.name: Make a live call to the provider and report the result

request.description:
Make a live call to the provider and report the result

`POST /v1/auth/admin/integrations/{provider}/test`

**Auth:** bearer token **plus the `admin:access` permission**. Sign in with the admin account or the gateway answers 403.

item.description:
Third-party credential registry. Requires `admin:access`.

Secrets are stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and are never returned in clear text — responses contain masked previews only. Saving a credential takes effect in the consuming service within ~30 seconds without a restart. Sending an empty string for a field clears it and falls back to the environment variable.

`POST .../test` runs a live call against the provider and reports whether the credentials actually work.

item.description:
Place search, reverse geocoding, saved places (Home/Work/Custom) and recent searches.

Results are served by a provider chain (Mapbox or Google, then an offline fallback) and cached in Redis, so a repeated search may be answered without calling the provider.

item.description:
Schema-driven table browser and editor, mounted by every service at `/v1/{segment}/admin/db`. Requires the `admin:access` permission.

The routes are generated from each service's Prisma schema, so the shape is identical everywhere and only the `:model` path parameter changes. Each subfolder below is pre-filled with a real model from that service.

Notes:
- Fields whose name looks sensitive (password, token, secret, otp, api key) are masked as `••••••` and cannot be edited.
- `PATCH` and `DELETE` identify the row by primary key in `where`.
- auth-service refuses to delete your own user row or the `super_admin` role.

item.name: 12 · Internal (service-to-service)

request.description:
Returns a provider's credentials **in clear text** for other services to consume.

`GET /v1/auth/internal/integrations/:provider`

**Auth:** the `x-internal-token` shared secret (`INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN`), not a JWT.

**This is not reachable through the gateway** — it targets auth-service directly on `{{authUrl}}`, because the gateway returns 404 for any `/v1/*/internal/**` path so credentials can never be relayed to the outside world.

This is how map-service resolves its Mapbox and Google keys and how ai-service resolves Gemini and ElevenLabs, which is why a key saved in the admin portal takes effect without a restart.

item.description:
Service-to-service endpoints. **The gateway deliberately returns 404 for these**, because they hand back credentials in clear text — they are reachable only on the internal network.

The request below therefore targets auth-service directly on `{{authUrl}}` and authenticates with the `x-internal-token` shared secret rather than a JWT. This is the mechanism other services use to resolve API keys at runtime.

It is excluded from Swagger on purpose, so it is written by hand here.
